summary: Low-priority webhook callbacks receiving intermittent 429s after enabling priority-smoothing
description:
Issue summary:
PacketWave started seeing intermittent 429s for low-rate webhook callback traffic after we enabled the platform feature 'priority-smoothing' for their dedicated pool. The 429s affect signed-url callback endpoints that are low qps but bursty, and appear only after smoothing is toggled on for the tenant.

Impact:
- ~3-7% of callback requests from PacketWave's ingestion pipelines are rejected with 429s during nightly micro-batches (00:00-01:00 UTC).
- Callbacks are critical for acknowledging storage uploads; failures trigger retries in PacketWave's system and cause duplicate processing and billing concerns.

Environment:
- Tenant: PacketWave Inc. (dedicated pool)
steps_to_reproduce: Enable 'priority-smoothing' flag on dedicated pool with default window=60s, smoothing_factor=0.6.
Send low-rate signed-url callback traffic: 0.2-1.5 rps per callback URL, burst to ~10 rps for short bursts (1-5s) every few minutes.
Observe callback response codes and X-RateLimit headers during nightly sweep window (00:00-01:30 UTC).
expected_behavior: Low-rate webhook callbacks should not receive 429s if overall tenant quota is available; smoothing should prevent oscillations and reduce transient rejects for background sweeps.
actual_behavior: A subset of callbacks receive 429 with response body 'rate limit exceeded'. Throttle headers returned show x-rate-limit-remaining: 0 and x-rate-limit-reset: short (1-6s). 429s correlate with priority-lane credit borrowing from interactive lanes during smoothing rebalancing.
logs_and_telemetry: Sample request id: req-20260310-7a9c2d (callback to /v1/signed-cb) - 429 - x-rl-remaining:0 - x-rl-reset:3
Ingress trace snippet (edge->origin): edge=edg-prod-11 us-east, origin=ded-pool-9, trace-id=tr-78f4. See trace in TraceUI: https://traces.redwood.dev/trace/tr-78f4
Rate-limiter metric graph: tenant/packetwave/prio-smoothing/borrow_count spiked series at 2026-03-10T00:04Z (see dashboard: https://console.redwood.dev/d/rl/priority-smoothing)
No 5xxs observed; only 429s. Billing counters show expected token consumption for successful retries.
temporary_workaround: Rollback: turning off 'priority-smoothing' on the tenant results in immediate reduction of callback 429s. PacketWave temporarily disabled smoothing overnight. Recommended short-term: remove smoothing flag for dedicated pool until mitigation is applied.
customer_notes: PacketWave team is concerned about duplicate ingestion and wants confirmation that smoothing won't cause billing over-count for retries. They requested an ETA for a fix and whether we can offer a per-route isolated burst lane for callbacks.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:18 - Maya Chen: Customer reports 429s started immediately after feature toggle; attached logs and sample req ids. Requested priority triage.

2026-03-10 11:02 - Liam O'Connor: Confirmed reproduction on dedicated sim env. Created linked investigation ticket INT-3321 for rate-limiter telemetry access. Asked engineering for hypothesis on credit borrowing behavior.

2026-03-10 14:40 - SRE (J. Patel): Initial hypothesis: smoothing reassigns refill credits between priority lanes on a 60s epoch; short signed-url bursts cause a lane to momentarily borrow credits then get penalized until reset. Asking for exact refill config and tenant weight.

2026-03-11 08:55 - Eng (R. Alvarez): Reviewed rate-limiter code path in PR #482 - smoothing makes borrow_count visible but doesn't isolate per-route burst pools. Proposed options: (A) add per-path burst exemption, (B) lower smoothing aggressiveness (smoothing_factor -> 0.3), (C) increase refill granularity to 10s windows.
2026-03-12 16:21 - Maya Chen: Customer accepted temporary rollback and asked for guidance on safe re-enable parameters and whether we can carve an isolated burst lane for their signed-url callbacks.

2026-03-12 18:00 - Liam O'Connor: Action item created: engineering to prototype per-route burst pool (EPIC INT-4100) and provide recommended smoothing parameters for PacketWave. Notified customer we'll follow up with tuning guidance and PR linking.
investigation_notes: Observed correlation between smoothing toggles and borrow_count spikes in tenant metrics.
Reproducer test in dedicated-sim confirmed 429s when smoothing enabled and many low-qps bursts present.
Rate-limiter currently accounts at tenant and priority-lane granularity; signed-URL callbacks share the same priority lane as low-latency interactive traffic in this tenant configuration.

Potential root cause: smoothing's ephemeral credit reallocation uses an epoch-based transfer that doesn't account for short-lived bursts that complete inside the transfer epoch, resulting in 'over-withdraw' and immediate 429s until next refill.
Edge case noted: health-checks and webhook replays during sweep may count as background flushes and accelerate refill depletion.
next_steps: Engineering to prototype per-route burst pool that can be opt-in for dedicated tenants (EPIC INT-4100).
Provide immediate tuning guidance: recommend smoothing_factor=0.25 and window=30s for PacketWave as a conservative re-enable setting.
Add monitoring alerts for borrow_count > 100/min and x-rl-429-rate > 0.5% during maintenance windows.

Confirm billing behavior on retries (finance asked that retries be flagged to avoid double-billing); coordinate with billing to mark callback retry tokens as retried-on-tenant for potential reimbursement policy.
Prepare a short runbook entry in Confluence documenting when to disable smoothing and how to configure per-route exemptions.
